armF.prompt:
Below is a finished English news feature article (already translated from Japanese, no section headings). Write ONE short, natural sentence that captures the core of the story, in a way a listener can understand by hearing it just once.

Requirements:
- Exactly one sentence.
- Understandable on a single listen.
- Do not pack in multiple separate points; focus on the single most important point or twist of the story.
- Do not add any new fact, conclusion, or lesson that is not already stated in the article below.
- Keep who did what to whom, and what exactly it applied to, the same as in the Japanese source article and the Ledger below.

As a rough guide only (Trial-only guidance, not a strict rule): aim for one main clause with at most one subordinate clause, roughly 12-18 words.

Output only the sentence itself, nothing else (no quotation marks, no label like "In one line:", no Markdown heading markup).

[Article]
# The Twist in AI Phone Calls: Who Was on the Other End?

Think of this story as a mystery, and there is one question: Who was actually speaking on the phone call handled by AI? Once you know the answer, it is harder to say, “As long as the task gets done, that’s good enough.”

Meta tested having trained human contract workers make some calls instead of AI and handle the conversation with the other person all the way through. In other words, the person speaking on the phone was human. If this were a play, a human helper had stepped in to play the AI. What we wonder as the audience is not just how well they acted. It is also: “Did you know who was playing the part?”

And the mystery does not end with who was on the other end of the phone. A person may need the user’s information to handle a task. Meta employees raised privacy concerns that sensitive information might be shared unintentionally with contract workers at call centers. This means that concerns were raised; it does not mean that a major leak happened. “A concern was raised” and “information was actually widely leaked” are two different things. Even readers playing detective should be careful not to mix them up.

The main point this time seems to be not that there was a human helper, but that the role changed without telling users. When you ask AI to handle a task, what does the AI do, and when do people step in? Whether you get to see the cast list first can affect how at ease you feel while watching.

Now for the solution. Meta’s vice president in charge admitted that starting a test in which contract workers made calls without properly informing users was a “mistake,” and the human concierge feature was temporarily rolled back. Muse as a whole was not stopped. What they stopped was the feature that let a person take over the phone call. In other words, the curtain came down not on AI as a whole, but on this feature where a person took over the call.

[Japanese source article]
AI電話のどんでん返し、受話器の向こうにいたのは誰？

今回の話、ミステリー仕立てで見ると、謎はひとつ。AIに頼んだ電話で、実際に話していたのは誰でしょう。答えを知ると、「用事が済めばそれでよし」とは言いにくくなります。

MetaのMuseでは、電話の一部をAIではなく、訓練を受けた人間の契約スタッフがかけ、相手とのやり取りを最後まで済ませるテストが行われていました。つまり、電話口で話していたのは人間だったのです。舞台でいえば、AIの役に人間の助っ人が登場。ここで観客として気になるのは、演技の出来だけではありません。「誰が演じているのか、聞いていた？」というところです。

そして謎は、電話の相手だけでは終わりません。人間が用事を進めるには、利用者の情報が必要になる場合があります。Metaの従業員からは、機微な情報がコールセンターの契約スタッフに意図せず共有されるかもしれない、というプライバシー上の懸念が出ていました。これは懸念が示されたという話で、大規模な情報漏えいが起きたという意味ではありません。「心配が出た」と「実際に広く漏れた」は別の話。ここは探偵役の読者も、取り違えないようにしたいところです。

人間の助っ人がいることより、利用者に知らせないまま役が入れ替わることが、今回のポイントに見えます。AIに用事を頼むとき、どこまでをAIが行い、どこから人が関わるのか。舞台の配役表を先に見せてもらえるかどうかは、安心して見ていられるかにも関わります。

さて、解決編です。Metaの担当副社長は、適切な開示をしないまま契約スタッフが電話をかけるテストを始めたのは「ミス」だったと認め、人間コンシェルジュ機能を当面ロールバックしました。Muse全体が止まったのではありません。止めたのは、電話を人間が代わる機能です。つまり幕が下りたのは、AI全体ではなく、人間が電話を代わるこの機能でした。

armR.final_summary: Meta rolled back Muse’s feature that let contract workers make calls after admitting users weren’t properly informed.
armR.final_text:
# The Twist in AI Phone Calls: Who Was on the Other End?

Think of this story as a mystery, and there is one question: Who was actually speaking on the phone call handled by AI? Once you know the answer, it is harder to say, “As long as the task gets done, that’s good enough.”

Meta tested having trained human contract workers make some calls instead of AI and handle the conversation with the other person all the way through. In other words, the person speaking on the phone was human. If this were a play, a human helper had stepped in to play the AI. What we wonder as the audience is not just how well they acted. It is also: “Did you know who was playing the part?”

And the mystery does not end with who was on the other end of the phone. A person may need the user’s information to handle a task. Meta employees raised privacy concerns that sensitive information might be shared unintentionally with contract workers at call centers. This means that concerns were raised; it does not mean that a major leak happened. “A concern was raised” and “information was actually widely leaked” are two different things. Even readers playing detective should be careful not to mix them up.

The main point this time seems to be not that there was a human helper, but that the role changed without telling users. When you ask AI to handle a task, what does the AI do, and when do people step in? Whether you get to see the cast list first can affect how at ease you feel while watching.

Now for the solution. Meta’s vice president in charge admitted that starting a test in which contract workers made calls without properly informing users was a “mistake,” and the human concierge feature was temporarily rolled back. Muse as a whole was not stopped. What they stopped was the feature that let a person take over the phone call. In other words, the curtain came down not on AI as a whole, but on this feature where a person took over the call.

## In one line
Meta rolled back Muse’s feature that let contract workers make calls after admitting users weren’t properly informed.
